lessons.title: Pinyin and tones
lessons.objective: Read pinyin, identify the four tones and pronounce basic syllables.

content.heading: What is pinyin?
content.text: Pinyin is the Latin-alphabet transcription of Chinese pronunciation. Each syllable combines an initial consonant and a final vowel, for example « ma », « ni », « hao ». It is the essential tool for beginners.

content.heading: The four tones
content.text: Chinese is a tonal language: the meaning changes with the tone. The first tone is high and flat (mā), the second rises (má), the third falls then rises (mǎ), the fourth falls sharply (mà). Example: « mā » (mother), « mà » (to scold).

content.heading: Practising the tones
content.text: To memorise, repeat each syllable with its tone while listening to audio models. The combination « nǐ hǎo » (hello) shows two third tones: the first is then pronounced in the second tone (ní hǎo).

exercises.question: How many tones does Mandarin have?
What does « mā » (first tone) mean?
How do you say "hello" in Chinese?

lessons.audioScript:
A: Nǐ hǎo! Wǒ jiào Lǐ Míng. Nǐ jiào shénme?
B: Wǒ jiào Wáng Lán. Nǐ hǎo!

lessons.title: Greetings
lessons.objective: Greet, take leave and exchange essential polite formulas.

content.heading: Greetings through the day
content.text: « Nǐ hǎo » (hello) is the universal greeting. In the morning say « zǎo shang hǎo » (good morning), and in the evening « wǎn shang hǎo » (good evening). Ask how someone is with « Nǐ hǎo ma? » (how are you?).

content.heading: Taking leave
content.text: To say goodbye: « zài jiàn » (goodbye). In the evening you can say « wǎn ān » (good night). To thank: « xiè xie » (thank you) and reply « bú kè qi » (you're welcome).

content.heading: Respect and titles
content.text: Chinese uses titles: « nín » (you, respectful form) and function titles like « lǎoshī » (teacher) or « xiānsheng » (Mr). The title is often added after the name: « Lǐ lǎoshī » (Teacher Li).

exercises.question: How do you say "thank you" in Chinese?
How do you answer "you're welcome"?
How do you say "goodbye"?

lessons.audioScript:
A: Zǎo shang hǎo, Lǐ lǎoshī!
B: Zǎo shang hǎo! Nǐ hǎo ma?
A: Wǒ hěn hǎo, xiè xie. Nín ne?
B: Wǒ yě hěn hǎo. Zài jiàn!

lessons.title: Numbers
lessons.objective: Count from 0 to 100 and give your phone number in Chinese.

content.heading: Basic numbers
content.text: The basic digits: líng (0), yī (1), èr (2), sān (3), sì (4), wǔ (5), liù (6), qī (7), bā (8), jiǔ (9), shí (10). Chinese counting can also be done in a particular way using one hand.

content.heading: Tens and compound numbers
content.text: The tens are formed simply: shí (10), èrshí (20), sānshí (30). For 11 to 19, say shí yī (11), shí èr (12), etc. For 21: èrshí yī (21), i.e. two-ten-one.

content.heading: The telephone
content.text: A phone number is read digit by digit, but « 1 » is often said « yāo » to avoid confusion. Example: 138 is said « yāo sān bā ».

exercises.question: How do you say 20 in Chinese?
How do you say 13?
Which digit is « bā »?

lessons.audioScript:
A: Nǐ de diàn huà hào mǎ shì duō shao?
B: Shì yāo sān bā, sì wǔ liù, qī bā jiǔ. Nǐ de ne?
A: Wǒ de shì shí èr sān sì wǔ liù.

lessons.title: The family
lessons.objective: Introduce your family and express possession with « de ».

content.heading: Family members
content.text: Family terms are very precise: bàba (father), māma (mother), gēge (older brother), dìdi (younger brother), jiějie (older sister), mèimei (younger sister). « Jiātíng » means the family.

content.heading: The extended family
content.text: The extended family distinguishes sides: yéye (paternal grandfather), nǎi nai (paternal grandmother), wàigōng (maternal grandfather), wàipó (maternal grandmother). « Wǒ jiā yǒu … » means "in my family there is …".

content.heading: Expressing possession
content.text: The particle « de » links the possessor and the object: wǒ de māma (my mother), nǐ de gēge (your older brother). To ask "whose?" say « shéi de? ».

exercises.question: How do you say "mother" in Chinese?
How do you say "my older brother"?
What does « yǒu » mean?

lessons.audioScript:
A: Nǐ jiā yǒu jǐ kǒu rén?
B: Wǒ jiā yǒu sì kǒu rén: bàba, māma, gēge hé wǒ. Nǐ ne?
A: Wǒ jiā yǒu wǔ kǒu rén.

lessons.title: Colours
lessons.objective: Name the colours and describe simple objects.

content.heading: Basic colours
content.text: Common colours: hóngsè (red), huángsè (yellow), lánsè (blue), lǜsè (green), báisè (white), hēisè (black). Add « sè » (colour) to the end of the base name.

content.heading: Saying your favourite colour
content.text: To express a taste: « wǒ xǐ huān hóngsè » (I like red). The negative: « wǒ bù xǐ huān hēisè » (I don't like black). « Nǐ xǐ huān shénme yánsè? » (which colour do you like?).

content.heading: Describing an object
content.text: The colour adjective follows the noun with « de »: yī jiàn hóngsè de yīfu (a red garment). The simple structure is: object + de + colour.

exercises.question: How do you say "red" in Chinese?
How do you say "I like blue"?
What does « shénme » mean?

lessons.audioScript:
A: Nǐ xǐ huān shénme yánsè?
B: Wǒ xǐ huān lánsè hé báisè. Nǐ ne?
A: Wǒ xǐ huān hóngsè. Hóngsè hěn hǎo kàn!

lessons.title: Food
lessons.objective: Order in a restaurant, name foods and use « qǐng » to ask politely.

content.heading: Foods and drinks
content.text: Around the table: mǐfàn (rice), miàntiáo (noodles), chá (tea), shuǐ (water), kāfēi (coffee), niúròu (beef), jī (chicken), yú (fish), cài (vegetables/dish). « Chīfàn » means to eat a meal.

content.heading: At the restaurant
content.text: To order: « wǒ yào … » (I want) or « qǐng gěi wǒ … » (please give me …). The bill: « mǎi dān » (the bill). The waiter asks: « Nǐ xiǎng chī shénme? » (what would you like to eat?).

content.heading: Chopsticks and politeness
content.text: « qǐng » is the polite word: qǐng jìn (please come in), qǐng zuò (please sit). To be polite, never stick chopsticks upright in the rice.

exercises.question: How do you say "rice" in Chinese?
How do you ask for the bill?
How do you say "I want"?

lessons.audioScript:
A: Nǐ xiǎng chī shénme?
B: Wǒ yào mǐfàn hé yú, qǐng.
A: Hǎo de. Nǐ yào hē shénme?
B: Yì bēi chá, qǐng.

lessons.title: Places
lessons.objective: Ask and say where places are in the city.

content.heading: Places in the city
content.text: Common places: xuéxiào (school), yīyuàn (hospital), shāngdiàn (shop), yínháng (bank), cāntīng (restaurant), huǒchēzhàn (station). « Qù » means to go: wǒ qù xuéxiào (I go to school).

content.heading: Asking where
content.text: To ask where a place is: « … zài nǎ li? » (where is …?). Example: « Huǒchēzhàn zài nǎ li? » (where is the station?). Answer: « zài zhèli » (here) or « zài nàli » (over there).

content.heading: Finding your way
content.text: Useful directions: zuǒ biān (left), yòu biān (right), qiánmiàn (in front), hòumiàn (behind), jìn (near). The way: « yì zhí zǒu » (go straight on).

exercises.question: How do you say "the hospital"?
How do you ask "where is the station?"
What does « yòu biān » mean?

lessons.audioScript:
A: Qǐng wèn, cāntīng zài nǎ li?
B: Cāntīng zài yòu biān, qiánmiàn.
A: Xiè xie! Zài yòu biān ma?
B: Shì de, zài yòu biān.

lessons.title: Time and dates
lessons.objective: Give the time, the days of the week and make an appointment.

content.heading: The time
content.text: Ask the time with « xiàn zài jǐ diǎn? » (what time is it?). The answer: « xiàn zài sān diǎn » (it is three o'clock). « Bàn » means half past: sān diǎn bàn (half past three).

content.heading: Days and time words
content.text: The days: xīngqī yī (Monday), xīngqī èr (Tuesday), … xīngqī tiān (Sunday). Time words: jīntiān (today), míngtiān (tomorrow), zuótiān (yesterday), xiàn zài (now).

content.heading: Making an appointment
content.text: « Shénme shíhou » means "at what time". Example: « Wǒmen jǐ diǎn jiànmiàn? » (what time shall we meet?). Answer: « wǒmen sān diǎn jiàn » (we meet at three).

exercises.question: How do you ask the time?
What does « sān diǎn bàn » mean?
Which day is « xīngqī tiān »?

lessons.audioScript:
A: Wǒmen jǐ diǎn jiàn miàn?
B: Wǒmen sān diǎn bàn jiàn, hǎo ma?
A: Sān diǎn bàn? Hǎo, míngtiān sān diǎn bàn jiàn!

lessons.title: Shopping
lessons.objective: Ask a price, bargain simply and buy items.

content.heading: Asking a price
content.text: In a shop ask: « Zhège duō shao qián? » (how much is this?). « Zhège » means "this" and « duō shao qián » means "how much money". The seller answers with the amount and « kuài » (yuan).

content.heading: Measure words
content.text: Chinese uses measure words depending on the object: « yī gè » for general objects, « yī běn shū » (a book), « yī jiàn yīfu » (a garment), « sān bēi chá » (three cups of tea).

content.heading: Buying and paying
content.text: To buy: « wǒ mǎi zhège » (I buy this). You can say « tài guì le » (too expensive) and « pián yi yī diǎn » (a bit cheaper). Payment: « xiànjīn » (cash) or « shuākǎ » (card).

exercises.question: How do you ask the price?
What does « tài guì le » mean?
How do you say "I buy this"?

lessons.audioScript:
A: Qǐng wèn, zhège duō shao qián?
B: Zhège shì wǔshí kuài.
A: Tài guì le! Pián yi yī diǎn, kě yǐ ma?
B: Hǎo, sìshí kuài.

lessons.title: Travel and transport
lessons.objective: Buy a ticket, use transport and understand travel information.

content.heading: Means of transport
content.text: Transport: chūzūchē (the taxi), gōnggòng qìchē (the bus), dìtiě (the metro), fēijī (the plane), huǒchē (the train). « Zuò » means to take transport: wǒ zuò dìtiě qù gōngsī (I take the metro to the office).

content.heading: Buying a ticket
content.text: At the counter: « mǎi yī zhāng piào » (buy a ticket). Specify the destination: « wǒ yào qù Běijīng » (I want to go to Beijing). « Liǎng zhāng piào » means two tickets.

content.heading: Departure
content.text: « Shénme shíhou chūfā? » (when do we leave?). The platform is « zhàntái ». The announcement: « huǒchē kuài yào kāi le » (the train is about to leave). « Wǎndiǎn » means the delay.

exercises.question: How do you say "the metro" in Chinese?
How do you say "two tickets"?
What does « wǎndiǎn » mean?

lessons.audioScript:
A: Qǐng wèn, huǒchē shén me shí hou chūfā?
B: Sān diǎn zhèng. Nǐ yào qù nǎ li?
A: Wǒ yào qù Shànghǎi. Mǎi yī zhāng piào, qǐng.
